options: Data produced by the machine-learning process of drawing conclusions, making predictions or generalising from a features dataset
The raw text of a document
A backup of the training data
questions.explanation: Inference data is what a model produces when it draws conclusions or predictions from analysed features.

questions.stem: In the school example, what does the smaller group of students you ask represent?
questions.explanation: Instead of asking every student, you ask a smaller, representative group — a sample.

questions.stem: In simple terms, inference is described as:
options: Asking every single person before deciding
Making smart guesses about everyone by looking at a few representative people first
Refusing to guess without complete data
Copying data from one system to another
questions.explanation: "I can figure out what most people like by asking a few of them, because they're probably a lot like everyone else."

questions.stem: Why does a sample allow useful conclusions about the whole group?
options: Because it is larger than the population
Because the sample is assumed to be representative of everyone else
Because it is stored in the cloud
questions.explanation: The representative few are "probably a lot like everyone else", which is what makes the generalisation reasonable.

questions.stem: Inference is described as a fundamental aspect of which discipline?
questions.explanation: Drawing conclusions about a larger dataset from observed data is fundamental to statistical reasoning and data analysis.

questions.stem: In machine learning, what is a trained model doing when it predicts on new, unseen data?
options: Generalising patterns learned from training data to new instances — an act of inference
questions.explanation: The model generalises what it learned from the training data to make predictions on new instances.

questions.stem: Which is a reason for using a sample rather than surveying everyone?
options: Asking every single person could be too much work
questions.explanation: Asking every student in a school could be too much work; a representative sample makes the task practical.

questions.stem: Inference often involves the application of what?
questions.explanation: Drawing meaningful conclusions from data often involves statistical methods.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between the features dataset and inference data?
options: Inference data is produced by analysing the features dataset
The features dataset is produced from inference data
Neither is used in machine learning
Inference data replaces the features dataset
questions.explanation: Conclusions and predictions (inference data) come from the analysis of the features dataset.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes inference from data?
options: It is a crucial step in extracting meaningful insights from data
It is an optional final formatting step
It is only relevant to spreadsheets
It requires no data at all
questions.explanation: Inference is a crucial step in extracting meaningful insights from data.
